criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Mission goal, four quantified objectives and a named user chain (GBRMPA, CSIRO/universities, BoM) are clearly linked to user needs, with literature support. Weaknesses: launch is not discussed, and the 'near-real-time' goal conflicts with the 24-hour delivery objective, so not full marks.

evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef
The satellite would be operated by the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS).

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt chart with weekly stages, justified task ordering tied to the mission logic, a risk and contingency table, and a planned information-source table. The plan is credible and feasible. Minor gaps are the absence of detail on launch-specific work and some inconsistency between the text and the Gantt for Week 10.

evidence.quote: so orbit work comes before ground control and communications, whose contact times depend on the chosen orbit
Relax objective 1 to fortnightly coverage, or assess a second satellite in the same orbit plane

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Table 3 gives correct, checkable hand calculations (period 5,801 s, 97.8° sun-synchronous inclination, 60 km swath), with interpretation that exposes the key design trade-off. The work is clearly on track. No STK output figures are shown, which keeps it from full marks.

evidence.quote: A first STK scenario with this orbit has been set up, and its period agrees with the hand calculation.
Weekly coverage (objective 1) is therefore not guaranteed by one satellite at this altitude and resolution.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear structure, labelled figure and tables, consistent IEEE-style references that are all cited. Language is mostly professional, but informal Gantt notes and a grammatical slip reduce polish, so the mark sits at the lower end of the level.

evidence.quote: Need to decide how to dispose/recycle the satellite after its lifespan
In 2016, a bleaching killed 30 percent of the reef’s coral.

technical_issues.issue: The goal calls for a near-real-time relay, but objective 3 allows delivery within 24 hours; these need reconciling.
The text says Week 10 has no new design work, yet the Gantt shows STK Simulations active in Week 10.
Launch is named as a planned task, but no launch vehicle, trajectory or site analysis is presented, so R2 is only partly addressed.
The bathymetry claim of 100 m per pixel is stated without a clear source or check.

overall: Strong, well-structured Part 1 report with a clear mission, credible plan and genuine preliminary orbit calculations that check out. Main gaps: launch analysis is missing, there is a near-real-time versus 24-hour inconsistency, and some informal wording. Marks are on the 0–10 level scale; weights (40/30/10/20) apply on conversion.

feedback.summary: You have produced a strong, well-structured Part 1 report with a clear mission, a credible plan and genuine preliminary orbit calculations that check out. Your concept links goals to named users, and your Gantt chart and risk table make the plan feasible. The main gaps are missing launch analysis, a near-real-time versus 24-hour inconsistency, and some informal wording.
next_steps: Add launch analysis covering the launch vehicle, trajectory and site, so the planned launch task is supported. This is what would fully address the partially met requirement R2.
Reconcile the near-real-time goal with objective 3's 24-hour delivery, and check that the Week 10 text matches the STK Simulations bar in Table 1 and Figure 1.

Source or verify the 100 m per pixel bathymetry figure in your concept section, and tidy informal wording such as 'Need to decide how to dispose/recycle the satellite' and the bleaching sentence in Preliminary Progress.

criteria.C1: Your goal, four quantified objectives and user chain (GBRMPA, CSIRO/universities, BoM) are clearly tied to user needs, with literature support. To push further, discuss launch within the mission concept and resolve the conflict between near-real-time delivery and the 24-hour objective, so requirements are consistent throughout.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart, weekly stages and reasoning for placing orbit work before ground control and communications make the plan credible. The risk and contingency table, including relaxing objective 1 to fortnightly coverage, is a strong touch. Strengthen it by adding launch-specific tasks and correcting the Week 10 mismatch between the text and Table 1 and Figure 1.
criteria.C3: Your hand calculations (5,801 s period, 97.8° sun-synchronous inclination, 60 km swath) are correct and checkable, and your interpretation of the weekly coverage trade-off shows real insight. Your STK scenario agreeing with the hand-calculated period is a good check. Adding brief STK output figures would make your evidence of progress even more convincing.
criteria.C4: Your report has a clear structure, labelled figures and tables, and consistently cited IEEE-style references. Language is mostly professional, but informal Gantt notes and a grammatical slip in the bleaching sentence reduce polish. Proofread for tone and grammar so the report reads at a fully professional level.
